critical_path.title: Successful Login with Valid Credentials
critical_path.description: Tests the successful login flow with valid username and password.
assertions: User is successfully logged in and redirected to their dashboard or profile page.

critical_path.title: Login Attempt with Invalid Password
critical_path.description: Tests the login failure scenario with an invalid password.
assertions: Error message is displayed indicating incorrect password or username. User remains on the login page.

validation.title: Login with Valid Username and Password
validation.description: Tests successful login with valid username and password.

steps.expected: Username field populated with valid username
Password field populated with valid password
User is redirected to the authenticated homepage or dashboard.

validation.title: Login with Empty Username and Password Fields
validation.description: Tests the validation of required fields for username and password, triggering error messages when submitted empty.

steps.expected: Form submission is prevented, and error messages are displayed.

assertions: Error messages are displayed indicating that both username and password are required.
The user remains on the login page.
Focus is set to first field (username) in error.

security.title: XSS Vulnerability in Username Field
security.description: This test attempts to inject a malicious JavaScript payload into the 'login_field' input to verify that the application properly sanitizes user inputs to prevent XSS attacks.

steps.action: Enter a JavaScript payload into the username field
steps.expected: The application should not execute the JavaScript code. The input should be properly escaped or sanitized.
The password field accepts and stores the value securely.
The login attempt should fail or be handled gracefully without executing the injected JavaScript.

assertions: The injected payload is not reflected in the DOM or any other part of the application's interface.
Login fails gracefully without any indication of successful injection or malicious code execution.

security.title: Authentication Bypass via SQL Injection in Username Field
security.description: This test attempts to bypass authentication by injecting a SQL injection payload into the 'login_field' input to check for vulnerabilities in the authentication process.

steps.action: Enter a SQL injection payload into the username field
steps.expected: The application should not allow SQL injection. The input should be properly sanitized or parameterized.
The password field accepts any value (dummy).
The login attempt should fail and the application should not be vulnerable to SQL injection. It must not allow login.

assertions: The system does not grant access based on the injection payload.
